L.N. 254 of 2026
CLIMATE ACTION ACT
(CAP. 643)
Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (Implementing)
Regulations, 2026
IN EXERCISE of the powers conferred by article 27 of the
Climate Action Act, the Minister responsible for climate action policy,
after consultation with the Climate Action Authority, has made the
following regulations:-
1. (1) The title of these regulations is the Carbon Border Citation and
scope.
Adjustment Mechanism (Implementing) Regulations, 2026.
(2) The scope of these regulations is to implement the
requirements of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 of the European Parliament
and of the Council of 10 May 2023 establishing a carbon border
adjustment mechanism, particularly the mechanism for the imposition
and enforcement of administrative penalties.
2. (1) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise Interpretation.
requires:
"Act" means the Climate Action Act; Cap. 643.
"Authority" means the Climate Action Authority as
established by article 9 of the Act;
"CBAM" means the Carbon Border Adjustment
Mechanism as established by Regulation (EU) 2023/956 of the
European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023
establishing a carbon border adjustment mechanism;
"Commission" means the European Commission;
"Directive 2003/87/EC" means Directive 2003/87/EC of
the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 October 2003
establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance
trading within the Community and amending Council Directive
96/61/EC;
"Regulation (EU) 2023/956" means Regulation (EU) 2023/
956 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May
2023 establishing a carbon border adjustment mechanism.
B 2794
B 2794
(2) Unless the context otherwise requires, the terms defined in
Regulation (EU) 2023/956 shall apply, and if any conflict arises the
provisions of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 shall prevail.
Applicability. 3. (1) These regulations shall apply to any authorised
CBAM declarant or any person falling within the scope of Regulation
(EU) 2023/956, including an authorised CBAM declarant, importer or
an authorised representative who is subject to obligations arising under
Regulation (EU) 2023/956, including obligations relating to reporting,
verification of embedded emissions, submission of CBAM
declarations and surrender of CBAM certificates.
(2) The provisions of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 shall apply
directly and shall be binding in their entirety, and these regulations
shall govern the enforcement, supervision and imposition of
administrative penalties in respect of an authorised CBAM declarant,
or any person falling within the scope of Regulation 2023/956.
Enforcement of 4. The Authority shall be the competent authority responsible
measures.
in exercising the enforcement measures established in these
regulations for the purposes of Article 11 of Regulation (EU) 2023/
956:
Provided that the Authority may, in accordance with the
Cap. 595.
Act and the Public Administration Act, delegate any of its functions to
any public officer or employee duly authorised for such purpose:
Provided further that the Authority shall, where necessary
for the purposes of Regulation (EU) 2023/956, cooperate and
exchange information with other public authorities in Malta, including
those responsible for customs, taxation and environmental protection,
as well as with competent authorities of other Member States and with
the Commission.
Accreditation of 5. The national accreditation body responsible for the
verifiers.
accreditation of verifiers for the purpose of these regulations,
including the verification of embedded emissions in accordance with
Articles 8 and 10 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 shall be the National
S.L. 419.07. Accreditation Board (Malta) as established by regulation 3 of the
National Accreditation Board (Malta) (Establishment) Regulations.
Administrative 6. (1) Any authorised CBAM declarant or person who fails
penalties.
to comply with any of the provisions of Regulation (EU) 2023/956
shall be liable to the measures and administrative penalties stipulated
in Article 16(3) and 16(4) of Directive 2003/87/EC and regulation 9(7)
S.L. 643.02. and (8) of the European Union Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading
System for Stationary Installations Regulations.

B 2795
(2) The Authority shall notify the authorised CBAM declarant
or the person in breach of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 in writing with
the administrative penalty imposed, by means of a judicial letter.
(3) The judicial letter referred to in sub-regulation (2) shall
include:
(a) a notice of the breach to comply with the obligations
of Regulation (EU) 2023/956;
(b) the reasons for such conclusion;
(c) the amount of the administrative penalty imposed;
(d) the date from when the penalty shall become due;
(e) the action to be taken for the payment of the
administrative penalty;
(f) the right of the authorised CBAM declarant or the
right of the person to appeal.
7. (1) Any person notified with a decision of the Authority Appeals.
under these regulations by means of a judicial letter as provided for in
regulation 6(2) may appeal such decision within twenty (20) days from
the date of service, before the Administrative Review Tribunal in Cap. 490.
accordance with the Administrative Justice Act.
(2) The decision of the Administrative Review Tribunal may
be appealed in accordance with articles 22 and 23 of the
Administrative Justice Act: Cap. 490.
(a) before the Court of Appeal in its Inferior Jurisdiction
in case of administrative penalties which do not exceed the
amount which the Court of Magistrates (Malta) is ratione valoris
competent to decide upon as indicated in article 47 of the Code Cap. 12.
of Organisation and Civil Procedure;
(b) before the Court of Appeal in its Superior Jurisdiction
in case of administrative penalties which exceed the amount
which the Court of Magistrates (Malta) is ratione valoris
competent to decide upon as indicated in article 47 of the Code Cap. 12.
of Organisation and Civil Procedure.
8. Administrative penalties which are not appealed before the Executive title.
Administrative Review Tribunal within the established period or
which are confirmed by the said Tribunal or by the Court of Appeal,
shall be deemed to constitute an executive title in accordance with Cap.12.
article 253 of the Code of Organisation and Civil Procedure.
